cd /app && cat > app/models/invitation.rb <<'EOF'
# An admin's invitation for someone to join the business as staff (an admin
# or an agent). The invitee gets an emailed link to the frontend, where they
# choose their name and password (see InvitationAcceptance).
#
# Statuses:
# * pending  - can be accepted until expires_at
# * accepted - the invitee joined the business; +user+ is who they became
# * revoked  - an admin withdrew it
# * expired  - it wasn't accepted in time; an admin can resend it
#
# A business never has two pending invitations for the same address, nor
# one for an address that already belongs to one of its users.
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  LIFETIME = 7.days
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze

  # Raised for resend/revoke requests that don't fit the invitation's status.
  class StateError < StandardError
    attr_reader :code

    def initialize(code, message)
      @code = code
      super(message)
    end
  end

  # Raised for links that can't be used (any more), with a message for the invitee.
  class InvalidToken < StandardError
    def initialize(message = "This invitation link is invalid. Ask an admin to send you a new one.")
      super
    end
  end

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true
  belongs_to :user, optional: true

  # Only staff are invited; customers sign up through the portal.
  enum :role, User::STAFF_ROLES.index_by(&:itself), validate: true, scopes: false

  normalizes :email, with: ->(email) { email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email, presence: true, length: { maximum: 254 },
    format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP, allow_blank: true }
  # Checked when an invitation is created or resent, under User.lock_email!.
  validate :email_is_available, on: [ :create, :resend ]

  # Neither accepted nor revoked; pending or expired depending on the time.
  scope :unanswered, -> { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :pending, ->(now = Time.current) { unanswered.where(expires_at: now..) }
  scope :expired, ->(now = Time.current) { unanswered.where(expires_at: ...now) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where.not(revoked_at: nil) }

  # The plain-text token for the emailed link. Only available right after
  # the invitation was created or resent.
  attr_reader :token

  def self.with_status(status, now = Time.current)
    case status
    when "pending" then pending(now)
    when "expired" then expired(now)
    when "accepted" then accepted
    when "revoked" then revoked
    else raise ArgumentError, "unknown invitation status #{status.inspect}"
    end
  end

  # Creates and returns an invitation; check +persisted?+ and +errors+.
  def self.invite(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:, now: Time.current)
    invitation = account.invitations.new(invited_by: invited_by, email: email, role: role)
    invitation.send(:issue_token, now)
    transaction do
      User.lock_email!(account.id, invitation.email) if invitation.email.present?
      invitation.save
    end
    invitation
  end

  # Finds the invitation an emailed +token+ belongs to, if it can still be
  # accepted. Otherwise raises InvalidToken (or Account::Cancelled).
  def self.find_acceptable!(token, account: nil, now: Time.current)
    raise InvalidToken if token.blank?

    invitation = find_by(token_digest: SecretToken.digest(token))
    raise InvalidToken if invitation.nil? || (account && invitation.account_id != account.id)

    invitation.ensure_acceptable!(token, now: now)
    invitation
  end

  def status(now = Time.current)
    if accepted_at
      "accepted"
    elsif revoked_at
      "revoked"
    elsif expires_at < now
      "expired"
    else
      "pending"
    end
  end

  def pending?(now = Time.current) = status(now) == "pending"
  def expired?(now = Time.current) = status(now) == "expired"
  def accepted? = accepted_at.present?
  def revoked? = revoked_at.present?

  def ensure_acceptable!(token, now: Time.current)
    raise InvalidToken unless token_digest == SecretToken.digest(token)

    case status(now)
    when "accepted" then raise InvalidToken, "This invitation has already been accepted. Sign in instead."
    when "revoked" then raise InvalidToken, "This invitation has been revoked."
    when "expired" then raise InvalidToken, "This invitation has expired. Ask an admin to send it again."
    end
    raise Account::Cancelled if account.cancelled?
  end

  # Sends a fresh link: the old one stops working and the invitation is
  # pending for another LIFETIME (which also revives an expired one).
  def resend!(now: Time.current)
    transaction do
      User.lock_email!(account_id, email)
      lock!
      raise StateError.new("invitation_already_accepted", "This invitation has already been accepted.") if accepted?
      raise StateError.new("invitation_revoked", "This invitation has been revoked. Send a new one instead.") if revoked?

      issue_token(now)
      save!(context: :resend)
    end
    self
  end

  # Withdraws the invitation so that its link stops working. Revoking a
  # revoked invitation changes nothing.
  def revoke!(now: Time.current)
    with_lock do
      raise StateError.new("invitation_already_accepted", "This invitation has already been accepted.") if accepted?

      update!(revoked_at: now) unless revoked?
    end
    self
  end

  private
    def issue_token(now)
      @token = SecretToken.generate
      self.token_digest = SecretToken.digest(@token)
      self.expires_at = now + LIFETIME
      self.sent_at = now
    end

    def email_is_available
      return if email.blank? || account.nil?

      if account.users.exists?(email: email)
        errors.add(:email, "already belongs to a user of this account")
      elsif account.invitations.pending.where.not(id: id).exists?(email: email)
        errors.add(:email, "already has a pending invitation")
      end
    end
end
EOF

# the ticket (for staff), while public_updated_at only moves for what the

# activity (notes, assignments) never changes the customer-facing request.
class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  # The staff member working on the ticket, if any.
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  # The database deletes comments together with their ticket.
  has_many :comments, class_name: "TicketComment", inverse_of: :ticket

  enum :status, { open: "open", pending: "pending", solved: "solved" }, validate: true, scopes: false

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(subject) { subject.to_s.squish }

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH }
  # Checked when the ticket is opened, so later changes to the user (such as a
  # new role) never make their existing tickets impossible to update.
  validate :requester_is_a_customer_of_the_account, on: :create
  validate :assignee_is_active_staff_of_the_account, if: -> { assignee_id.present? && will_save_change_to_assignee_id? }

  before_create :start_public_activity

  # Recently active first, as staff see them. Every reply, note, status
  # change and assignment bumps updated_at.
  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  # Recently active first, as the requester sees them.
  scope :recently_active_in_public, -> { order(public_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  private
    def requester_is_a_customer_of_the_account
      return if requester.nil? || account_id.nil?

      errors.add(:requester, "must be a customer of this account") unless
        requester.customer? && requester.account_id == account_id
    end

    def assignee_is_active_staff_of_the_account
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member of this account") unless
        assignee && assignee.account_id == account_id && assignee.active_staff?
    end

    # A new ticket's activity so far is all public.
    def start_public_activity
      now = current_time_from_proper_timezone
      self.created_at ||= now
      self.updated_at ||= created_at
      self.public_updated_at ||= updated_at
    end
end

# A reply, status change and/or assignment on a ticket, either by its
# requester (through /requests) or by staff (through /tickets).
#
# Status rules:
# * Staff can set any status. A staff comment on its own leaves the status alone.
# * Customers can only mark their request solved. A customer's comment reopens a
#   pending or solved request, unless the same update marks it solved.
#
# Customers' comments are always public; staff comments are public unless
# they say "public": false (an internal note).
#
# Only staff assign tickets, to active staff of the business (or nobody).
#
# Every change bumps the ticket's updated_at, but only public comments and
# status changes bump public_updated_at, which is what the requester sees.
class TicketUpdate
  include FormErrors

  BOOLEANS = { true => true, false => false, "true" => true, "false" => false }.freeze
  # Default for +assignee_id+: the update doesn't touch the assignment.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze
  MAX_ID = 2**63 - 1

  attr_reader :ticket, :comment, :errors

  # +status+ is nil when the update doesn't ask for a status; +comment+ is
  # nil when it doesn't include a comment, or a hash with "body" (and, for
  # staff, "public"). +assignee_id+ is a user ID, or nil to unassign.
  def initialize(ticket, author:, status: nil, comment: nil, assignee_id: UNCHANGED)
    @ticket = ticket
    @author = author
    @requested_status = status
    @comment_attributes = comment&.to_h&.with_indifferent_access
    @requested_assignee = assignee_id
    @errors = {}
  end

  def save
    Ticket.transaction do
      # The new assignee is locked before the ticket, in the same order as
      # User#suspend!, so nobody can suspend them (and so unassign their
      # tickets) until this update is committed.
      new_assignee = lock_new_assignee if assigning?
      # Lock the ticket so that concurrent updates apply their status rules
      # one after the other, each to the current status.
      ticket.lock!
      now = Time.current
      @comment = build_comment(now) if @comment_attributes
      new_status = resulting_status
      next unless valid?(new_assignee)

      ticket.status = new_status
      ticket.assignee = new_assignee if assigning?
      ticket.updated_at = now if comment || ticket.changed?
      ticket.public_updated_at = now if comment&.public? || ticket.status_changed?
      comment&.save!
      ticket.save! if ticket.changed?
    end
    errors.empty?
  end

  private
    attr_reader :author, :requested_status

    def assigning?
      !@requested_assignee.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    end

    def build_comment(now)
      TicketComment.new(ticket: ticket, author: author, body: @comment_attributes[:body], public: comment_public?,
        created_at: now, updated_at: now)
    end

    # Only exact booleans are accepted (an unrecognised value such as "no"
    # leaves nil, which fails validation) so that an internal note is never
    # published by accident.
    def comment_public?
      return true if author.customer?

      value = @comment_attributes[:public]
      value.nil? ? true : BOOLEANS.fetch(value, nil)
    end

    def resulting_status
      if author.customer?
        if requested_status == "solved"
          "solved"
        elsif comment && (ticket.pending? || ticket.solved?)
          "open"
        else
          ticket.status
        end
      else
        requested_status || ticket.status
      end
    end

    # The requested assignee, locked against concurrent suspension, or nil
    # when unassigning (or when there's no such user in the business).
    def lock_new_assignee
      id = requested_assignee_id or return nil

      ticket.account.users.lock("FOR SHARE").find_by(id: id)
    end

    def requested_assignee_id
      id = case @requested_assignee
      when Integer then @requested_assignee
      when /\A\s*\d+\s*\z/ then @requested_assignee.to_i
      end
      id if id&.between?(1, MAX_ID)
    end

    def valid?(new_assignee)
      @errors = {}
      if requested_status
        if author.customer?
          @errors["status"] = [ "can only be changed to solved" ] unless requested_status == "solved"
        elsif !Ticket.statuses.key?(requested_status)
          @errors["status"] = [ "is not included in the list" ]
        end
      end
      if assigning?
        if author.customer?
          @errors["assignee_id"] = [ "can only be changed by staff" ]
        elsif !@requested_assignee.nil? && !new_assignee&.active_staff?
          @errors["assignee_id"] = [ "must be an active staff member of this account" ]
        end
      end
      if comment
        comment.validate
        @errors.merge!(collect_errors(comment.errors, prefix: "comment.", except: [ :ticket ]))
      end
      @errors.empty?
    end
end
EOF

module Api
  module V1
    # Admins invite new staff (admins and agents) and manage the invitations.
    class InvitationsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_admin!
      before_action :set_invitation, only: [ :show, :resend, :destroy ]

      # Every invitation sends an email, so limit how many a business sends.
      rate_limit to: 100, within: 1.hour, only: [ :create, :resend ], name: "invitation-emails",
        by: -> { Current.account.id },
        with: -> { render_too_many_requests(retry_after: 1.hour) }

      # GET /api/v1/invitations?status=pending
      def index
        invitations = Current.account.invitations.includes(:invited_by).order(:id)
        if (status = list_filter(:status, Invitation::STATUSES))
          invitations = invitations.with_status(status)
        end
        render_page invitations, :invitations, InvitationSerializer
      end

      # GET /api/v1/invitations/:id
      def show
        render json: { invitation: InvitationSerializer.call(@invitation) }
      end

      # POST /api/v1/invitations
      def create
        attributes = params.expect(invitation: [ :email, :role ])
        invitation = Invitation.invite(account: Current.account, invited_by: Current.user,
          email: attributes[:email], role: attributes[:role])
        return render_validation_errors(invitation.errors) unless invitation.persisted?

        deliver_invitation(invitation)
        render json: { invitation: InvitationSerializer.call(invitation) }, status: :created
      end

      # POST /api/v1/invitations/:id/resend - emails a new link (the old one
      # stops working) and restarts the expiry, also for expired invitations.
      def resend
        @invitation.resend!
        deliver_invitation(@invitation)
        render json: { invitation: InvitationSerializer.call(@invitation) }
      end

      # DELETE /api/v1/invitations/:id - revokes the invitation. It stays in
      # the list with the status "revoked".
      def destroy
        @invitation.revoke!
        render json: { invitation: InvitationSerializer.call(@invitation) }
      end

      private
        def set_invitation
          @invitation = Current.account.invitations.find_by(id: params[:id]) or render_not_found(:invitation)
        end

        def deliver_invitation(invitation)
          deliver_email InvitationMailer.with(invitation: invitation, token: invitation.token).invitation
        end
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class InvitationsTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_up_verified
    @owner_token = sign_in
    @owner = User.find_by!(email: "jo@acme.test")
    @account = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme")
  end

  def preview(token, account: nil)
    api :post, "/invitation_previews", { invitation_preview: { token: token } }, account: account
  end

  def accept(token, name: "Sam", password: STAFF_PASSWORD, account: nil)
    api :post, "/invitation_acceptances", { invitation_acceptance: { token: token, name: name, password: password } },
      account: account
  end

  test "an admin invites an agent, who previews the invitation, accepts it and signs in" do
    invitation = nil
    assert_emails 1 do
      invitation = invite(@owner_token, email: " Sam@Example.TEST ", role: "agent")
    end

    assert_kind_of Integer, invitation["id"]
    assert_equal({ "account_id" => @account.id, "email" => "sam@example.test", "role" => "agent", "status" => "pending",
                   "invited_by_id" => @owner.id, "invited_by" => { "id" => @owner.id, "name" => "Jo" }, "user_id" => nil,
                   "accepted_at" => nil, "revoked_at" => nil },
      invitation.slice("account_id", "email", "role", "status", "invited_by_id", "invited_by", "user_id", "accepted_at", "revoked_at"))
    assert_in_delta 7.days.from_now, Time.zone.parse(invitation["expires_at"]), 1.minute
    assert_not invitation.key?("token")

    assert_equal [ "sam@example.test" ], last_email.to
    assert_includes last_email.subject, "Acme"
    token = emailed_token("accept-invitation")
    assert_includes last_email.text_part.body.decoded, "http://localhost:3001/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=#{token}"
    assert_includes last_email.text_part.body.decoded, "Jo has invited you"
    assert_not Invitation.exists?(token_digest: token), "only a digest of the token is stored"

    preview(token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal({ "email" => "sam@example.test", "role" => "agent", "account_name" => "Acme", "subdomain" => "acme",
                   "expires_at" => invitation["expires_at"] },
      json["invitation_preview"].slice("email", "role", "account_name", "subdomain", "expires_at"))

    assert_no_emails do
      accept(token)
    end
    assert_response :created
    user = json.fetch("user")
    assert_equal({ "account_id" => @account.id, "name" => "Sam", "email" => "sam@example.test", "role" => "agent",
                   "owner" => false, "verified" => true, "suspended" => false },
      user.slice("account_id", "name", "email", "role", "owner", "verified", "suspended"))
    assert_equal "acme", json.dig("account", "subdomain")

    # No verification email needed.
    agent_token = sign_in(email: "sam@example.test", password: STAFF_PASSWORD)
    api :get, "/tickets", token: agent_token
    assert_response :ok

    api :get, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}", token: @owner_token
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "accepted", json.dig("invitation", "status")
    assert_equal user["id"], json.dig("invitation", "user_id")
    assert json.dig("invitation", "accepted_at").present?
  end

  test "an invited admin can manage people" do
    admin_token = sign_in_invited(@owner_token, email: "ada@example.test", role: "admin", name: "Ada")

    api :get, "/me", token: admin_token
    assert_equal "admin", json.dig("user", "role")
    invite(admin_token, email: "kim@example.test")
    api :get, "/users", token: admin_token
    assert_response :ok
  end

  test "an invitation link works once" do
    invite(@owner_token)
    token = emailed_token("accept-invitation")
    accept(token)
    assert_response :created

    [ -> { preview(token) }, -> { accept(token, name: "Mallory") } ].each do |attempt|
      attempt.call
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
      assert_equal "invalid_token", json.dig("error", "code")
      assert_match(/already been accepted/, json.dig("error", "message"))
    end
    assert_equal 1, User.where(email: "sam@example.test").count
  end

  test "accepting needs a name and a valid password, and leaves the link usable otherwise" do
    invite(@owner_token)
    token = emailed_token("accept-invitation")

    assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
      accept(token, name: " ", password: "short")
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal "validation_failed", json.dig("error", "code")
    assert_equal %w[name password], json.dig("error", "details").keys.sort

    accept(token, password: "")
    assert_equal [ "can't be blank" ], json.dig("error", "details", "password")

    api :post, "/invitation_acceptances", {}
    assert_response :bad_request

    accept(token)
    assert_response :created
  end

  test "unknown, revoked, replaced and expired links are rejected" do
    [ "", "nope" ].each do |token|
      preview(token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
      assert_equal "invalid_token", json.dig("error", "code")
      accept(token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
    end

    invitation = invite(@owner_token)
    first_token = emailed_token("accept-invitation")
    api :post, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}/resend", token: @owner_token
    assert_response :ok
    second_token = emailed_token("accept-invitation")
    assert_not_equal first_token, second_token

    preview(first_token)
    assert_response :unprocessable_content, "resending replaces the link"
    preview(second_token)
    assert_response :ok

    travel Invitation::LIFETIME + 1.minute do
      preview(second_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
      assert_match(/expired/, json.dig("error", "message"))
      accept(second_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
      api :get, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}", token: sign_in
      assert_equal "expired", json.dig("invitation", "status")
    end

    api :delete, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}", token: @owner_token
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "revoked", json.dig("invitation", "status")
    preview(second_token)
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_match(/revoked/, json.dig("error", "message"))
    assert_not User.exists?(email: "sam@example.test")
  end

  test "resending emails a new link and revives an expired invitation" do
    invitation = invite(@owner_token)

    travel Invitation::LIFETIME + 1.day do
      admin_token = sign_in
      assert_emails 1 do
        api :post, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}/resend", token: admin_token
      end
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal "pending", json.dig("invitation", "status")
      assert_in_delta Invitation::LIFETIME.from_now, Time.zone.parse(json.dig("invitation", "expires_at")), 1.minute
      assert Time.zone.parse(json.dig("invitation", "sent_at")) > Time.zone.parse(invitation["sent_at"])

      accept_invitation
    end
  end

  test "revoking" do
    invitation = invite(@owner_token)

    api :delete, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}", token: @owner_token
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "revoked", json.dig("invitation", "status")
    assert json.dig("invitation", "revoked_at").present?

    # Revoking again changes nothing; resending is refused.
    api :delete, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}", token: @owner_token
    assert_response :ok
    assert_no_emails do
      api :post, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}/resend", token: @owner_token
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal "invitation_revoked", json.dig("error", "code")

    # A revoked invitation doesn't hold the address.
    invite(@owner_token)
    accept_invitation

    accepted = Invitation.find_by!(email: "sam@example.test", accepted_at: ..Time.current)
    [ [ :delete, "" ], [ :post, "/resend" ] ].each do |method, suffix|
      api method, "/invitations/#{accepted.id}#{suffix}", token: @owner_token
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
      assert_equal "invitation_already_accepted", json.dig("error", "code")
    end
  end

  test "invitations are validated" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Invitation.count } do
      assert_no_emails do
        api :post, "/invitations", { invitation: { email: "nope", role: "customer" } }, token: @owner_token
      end
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal "validation_failed", json.dig("error", "code")
    assert_equal({ "email" => [ "is invalid" ], "role" => [ "is not included in the list" ] }, json.dig("error", "details"))

    api :post, "/invitations", { invitation: { email: "sam@example.test" } }, token: @owner_token
    assert_equal [ "is not included in the list" ], json.dig("error", "details", "role")

    api :post, "/invitations", {}, token: @owner_token
    assert_response :bad_request
  end

  test "no competing invitations, and none for existing users" do
    invite(@owner_token, role: "agent")
    register_customer

    [ [ "SAM@example.test", "already has a pending invitation" ],
      [ "jo@acme.test", "already belongs to a user of this account" ],
      [ "avery@example.test", "already belongs to a user of this account" ] ].each do |email, message|
      assert_no_difference -> { Invitation.count } do
        api :post, "/invitations", { invitation: { email: email, role: "admin" } }, token: @owner_token
      end
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
      assert_equal [ message ], json.dig("error", "details", "email")
    end

    # Other businesses are unaffected.
    sign_up_verified(subdomain: "globex", name: "Globex", email: "boss@globex.test")
    invite(sign_in(email: "boss@globex.test", account: "globex"), email: "sam@example.test", account: "globex")
  end

  test "an expired invitation doesn't hold the address, but can't be revived next to a newer one" do
    old = invite(@owner_token)

    travel Invitation::LIFETIME + 1.minute do
      admin_token = sign_in
      newer = invite(admin_token, role: "admin")
      assert_not_equal old["id"], newer["id"]

      api :post, "/invitations/#{old["id"]}/resend", token: admin_token
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
      assert_equal [ "already has a pending invitation" ], json.dig("error", "details", "email")
      assert_equal 1, Invitation.pending.where(email: "sam@example.test").count
    end
  end

  test "customers can't register with the address of a pending invitation" do
    invitation = invite(@owner_token)

    assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
      api :post, "/registrations", { user: { name: "Sam", email: "Sam@example.test", password: CUSTOMER_PASSWORD } }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal [ "has already been taken" ], json.dig("error", "details", "email")

    # Once it's no longer pending, the address is free again.
    api :delete, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}", token: @owner_token
    register_customer(name: "Sam", email: "sam@example.test")

    api :post, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}/resend", token: @owner_token
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
  end

  test "an invitation for an address that registered after it expired can't be resent" do
    invitation = invite(@owner_token)

    travel Invitation::LIFETIME + 1.minute do
      register_customer(name: "Sam", email: "sam@example.test")
      api :post, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}/resend", token: sign_in
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
      assert_equal [ "already belongs to a user of this account" ], json.dig("error", "details", "email")
    end
  end

  test "listing invitations by ID, filtered by status" do
    pending = invite(@owner_token, email: "pending@example.test")
    accepted = invite(@owner_token, email: "accepted@example.test")
    accept_invitation
    revoked = invite(@owner_token, email: "revoked@example.test")
    api :delete, "/invitations/#{revoked["id"]}", token: @owner_token
    expired = travel_to(8.days.ago) { invite(@owner_token, email: "expired@example.test") }

    api :get, "/invitations", token: @owner_token
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ pending, accepted, revoked, expired ].pluck("id").sort, json["invitations"].pluck("id")
    assert_equal({ "count" => 4, "page" => 1, "per_page" => 25, "next_page" => nil, "previous_page" => nil },
      json.except("invitations"))

    { "pending" => pending, "accepted" => accepted, "revoked" => revoked, "expired" => expired }.each do |status, invitation|
      api :get, "/invitations?status=#{status}", token: @owner_token
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal [ invitation["id"] ], json["invitations"].pluck("id"), status
      assert_equal [ status ], json["invitations"].pluck("status")
    end

    api :get, "/invitations?per_page=2&page=2", token: @owner_token
    assert_equal [ revoked, expired ].pluck("id"), json["invitations"].pluck("id")

    api :get, "/invitations?status=lost", token: @owner_token
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal({ "status" => [ "is not included in the list" ] }, json.dig("error", "details"))
  end

  test "only admins manage invitations" do
    invitation = invite(@owner_token)
    agent_token = sign_in_invited(@owner_token, email: "agent@example.test")
    customer_token = sign_in_new_customer

    [ agent_token, customer_token ].each do |token|
      [ [ :get, "/invitations" ], [ :get, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}" ], [ :post, "/invitations" ],
        [ :post, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}/resend" ], [ :delete, "/invitations/#{invitation["id"]}" ] ].each do |method, path|
        api method, path, { invitation: { email: "x@example.test", role: "admin" } }, token: token
        assert_response :forbidden
        assert_equal "forbidden", json.dig("error", "code")
      end
    end
    assert_equal "pending", Invitation.find(invitation["id"]).status
  end

  test "other businesses' invitations are not found, and their links don't work here" do
    invite(@owner_token)
    token = emailed_token("accept-invitation")
    sign_up_verified(subdomain: "globex", name: "Globex", email: "boss@globex.test")
    globex_token = sign_in(email: "boss@globex.test", account: "globex")
    id = Invitation.last.id

    [ [ :get, "" ], [ :post, "/resend" ], [ :delete, "" ] ].each do |method, suffix|
      api method, "/invitations/#{id}#{suffix}", account: "globex", token: globex_token
      assert_response :not_found
    end

    preview(token, account: "globex")
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    accept(token, account: "globex")
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    preview(token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
  end

  test "invitations of a cancelled business can't be used" do
    invite(@owner_token)
    token = emailed_token("accept-invitation")
    @account.cancel!

    [ -> { preview(token) }, -> { accept(token) }, -> { accept(token, account: "acme") } ].each do |attempt|
      attempt.call
      assert_response :forbidden
      assert_equal "account_cancelled", json.dig("error", "code")
    end
    assert_not User.exists?(email: "sam@example.test")
  end
end

require "test_helper"

# Races between requests, each in its own thread and database connection.
# The first transaction is held open until the second one is known to be
# waiting for it, so these are deterministic. They commit for real, so they
# can't use transactional tests.
class ConcurrencyTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  self.use_transactional_tests = false

  setup do
    registration = AccountRegistration.new(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme",
      admin: { name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "password-123" })
    assert registration.save
    @account = registration.account
    @owner = registration.user
  end

  teardown { Account.delete_all }

  # Runs +first+ in a transaction that stays open until +second+ (started
  # meanwhile in another thread) is blocked on it. Returns both results (or
  # the exceptions they raised).
  def race(first, second)
    holding = Queue.new
    release = Queue.new
    first_thread = Thread.new do
      ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          result = capture(&first)
          holding << true
          release.pop
          result
        end
      end
    end
    holding.pop
    second_thread = Thread.new { ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection { capture(&second) } }
    sleep 0.1 until second_thread.status == "sleep" || !second_thread.alive?
    sleep 0.2 # Let it reach the lock.
    assert second_thread.alive?, "expected the second transaction to wait for the first"
    release << true
    [ first_thread.value, second_thread.value ]
  end

  def capture
    yield
  rescue => error
    error
  end

  def add_user(email, role:)
    @account.users.create!(name: email.split("@").first.capitalize, email: email, password: "password-123",

steps.message:
Everything in the issue is implemented. The full suite passes (145 tests, stable across repeated runs), and I ran the whole flow end to end against a real Puma server with curl.

**Two things were already partly there:**
- The `agent` role already existed in the code. I added a database constraint so only `admin`, `agent` and `customer` can be stored.
- Private notes already worked through the comment input, but they changed the customer's request: each note updated its `updated_at` and moved it up the customer's list. Tickets now keep a second, customer-facing timestamp that only public comments and status changes update. Notes and assignments leave the customer's request exactly as it was; staff still see all activity on their side.

**What's new**
- **Invitations:** all the endpoints you listed, with emailed `/accept-invitation?account=…&token=…` links, preview and acceptance. Invitees can sign in straight away without a verification email. Each business has at most one pending invitation per address, and none for an address that already belongs to one of its users. Customers can't register with an address that has a pending invitation.
- **People:** `GET/PATCH /users` with role and suspension filters, plus `GET /staff`, both listed by ID. Suspension signs the user out, cancels their emailed links and unassigns their tickets. Suspended users can't sign in (`403 user_suspended`) or be assigned tickets. Nobody can suspend the last active admin.
- **Assignment:** `assignee_id` can be set or cleared with `null`, and tickets include `assignee_id` and `assignee: {id, name}`. Only active staff of the same business can be assigned. A single update can combine a comment, a status and an assignment; if any part is invalid, nothing changes.
- **Concurrency:** simultaneous requests are handled safely, e.g. two admins suspending each other, two identical invitations, or a registration racing an invitation. Thread-based tests cover these, and I checked that they fail when the protection is removed.
- **Docs:** the README covers the new endpoints, response shapes, error codes and rules.

**Choices the spec didn't settle, worth checking**
- `DELETE /invitations/:id` returns 200 with the invitation marked `revoked` rather than 204, because the record stays in the list.
- Accepting an invitation returns 201, since it creates a user.
- The preview shows the business as both `account_name` and `account: {name, subdomain}`, because the spec didn't name the field. I can drop one.
- Invitations expire after 7 days. Resending sends a new link and also revives an expired invitation, unless someone has taken the address in the meantime.
- Invitation emails are limited to 100 per hour per business.
- The account owner can be suspended like any admin, as long as they aren't the last active one. Protecting the owner is a one-line change if you'd rather.
- `PATCH /users/:id` only accepts `suspended`; changing someone's role isn't supported.

**Changes to existing tests:** two ticket-shape assertions now include the assignee fields. The database foreign-key test now also checks the new `assignee_id` column, which is deferred like the ticket's other references to users.

The rake-task test in `account_test.rb` fails when that file is run on its own, because Rake isn't loaded. It passes in the full suite, and it fails the same way without my changes.
steps.reasoning_content:
Everything looks stable now, so I'm putting together a summary for the user covering the judgment calls made: the agent role already existed but I added a DB constraint, internal notes needed a public_updated_at fix to avoid leaking changes to customers, and I made decisions like returning 200 with the revoked invitation on delete, 201 on acceptance, and handling preview keys appropriately.

I should also flag that the owner isn't protected from suspension beyond the last-admin rule since that's spec-literal, note the invitation lifetime and rate limits, mention that resend revives expired invitations, and call out the existing test changes plus the pre-existing flaky rake task and that role changes aren't supported in the PATCH endpoint.
